sources.design: RCT, 41 participants; underpowered relative to planned definitive sample
sources.population: Age 12–35, nontraumatic/nonstructural MDI, MRI exclusion of structural lesions.
sources.comparator: Watson staged scapular-control program versus Rockwood cuff/deltoid program.
sources.coInterventions: Education and home exercises; other care/medications recorded.
sources.outcomes: At 24 weeks WOSI difference 12.6, MISS 15.4, pain −2.0 favored Watson; no meaningful difference demonstrated for dislocation incidence.
sources.followUp: 6, 12, 24 weeks; longer follow-up planned, not reported here.
sources.uncertainty: Small sample, several authors teach/work in program-associated services; no no-treatment group or isolated-exercise effect.
sources.harms: 14 minor postexercise soreness events (5 Watson/9 Rockwood), resolved with 48-hour rest/modification; no serious events reported.
sources.limitations: Not traumatic structural instability, repair or unrestricted gym clearance.

protocol.execution: Watson: clinician-specific scapular control, standing band ER 0–45° at 0° abduction, rows, later side-lying ER/functional ranges. Rockwood includes wall/knee/full push-ups and cuff/deltoid work.
protocol.dose: Watson typical recruitment 3×20 then endurance 3×10–15 and later strength 4×8–12; most holds 3 seconds. Rockwood 5 reps with 5-sec end-range hold. Study extraction only.
protocol.frequency: Watson recruitment/endurance typically twice daily, later strength alternate days; Rockwood twice daily.
protocol.supervision: Weekly 30-min physiotherapy for 12 weeks, trained therapists with fidelity checks.
protocol.progression: Watson progressed load/elevation after pain-free scapular/GH control for full exercise set; Rockwood increased resistance when relatively easy.
protocol.stoppingRules: Exercises performed pain free in both programs; soreness events managed by rest/modification. These do not establish universal damage or rest-duration rules.

locations: Methods > Participants and Recruitment; Interventions; Table 1 (PDF pp. 2–4)

sources.population: First-time radiologically confirmed anterior traumatic dislocation, mean age45, managed nonoperatively; neurovascular complications/bilateral injury/surgical candidates excluded.
sources.comparator: Single advice/materials/self-referral option versus same plus extra PT.
sources.coInterventions: Both groups progressive-exercise education and initial sling-supported period.
sources.outcomes: Six-month Oxford instability difference 1.5 (95% CI −0.3 to 3.5), no worthwhile extra-PT superiority; similar complications, ten redislocations overall.
sources.uncertainty: 73% primary follow-up; not a young collision-athlete-only trial.
sources.harms: Similar complication profiles; no significant group difference.
sources.limitations: Not no rehabilitation, recurrent structural instability or immediate unrestricted return.

protocol.execution: Initial therapist exam/advice with progressive exercise materials; exact individual execution not extracted from linked booklet.
protocol.dose: Advice up to 1 hour; extra PT up to 30-min sessions over maximum four months.
protocol.frequency: not reported as common per-exercise frequency in inspected main text.
protocol.supervision: Initial physiotherapist session within six weeks in both arms; extra sessions in experimental arm.
protocol.progression: Patient education/exercise planning; no generic release date.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as a numeric exercise-specific autonomous stopping rule.
